lineage_context.teaching_goal: Separate the Portulaca-style succulent flower and circumscissile capsule from closely related Talinaceae and other Caryophyllales.

project_scope.note: The current pool contains only Portulaca; this makes the family lesson unusually clean and genus-centered.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a succulent herb with simple fleshy leaves, usually 2 sepals, 4–6 showy petals, and a one-celled many-ovuled ovary. The best confirmation is the capsule opening circumscissilely like a lid.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual or perennial succulent herbs; stems erect to prostrate. Leaves alternate, opposite or subopposite, fleshy; axillary hairs may occur.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and radial, often terminal or surrounded by a cluster of upper leaves. Sepals usually 2; petals usually 4–6; stamens often numerous.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A many-seeded capsule, especially in Portulaca opening circumscissilely so the top separates like a lid.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Confirm the two-sepal flower and many-seeded circumscissile capsule. Talinum capsules split longitudinally; some Amaranthus fruits also open by a lid, so seed count and perianth matter.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: succulent habit → 2 sepals/5-ish petals → circumscissile capsule → Talinaceae contrast
visual_lesson.intro: Portulacaceae is the 'lid-opening capsule' branch of this Caryophyllales neighborhood.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the succulent Portulaca habit
steps.look_for: Prostrate or spreading fleshy stems and simple succulent leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fast gestalt, but fruit is the real confirmation.

steps.title: 2 · Count the sepals
steps.look_for: Usually two sepals beneath a 4–6-petaled flower, often with many stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: The 2-sepal plan is shared with Talinaceae and sets up the close-family comparison.

steps.title: 3 · Find the lid-opening capsule
steps.look_for: The capsule splits around its circumference, leaving a lower cup and a removable cap.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest local Portulaca/Portulacaceae teaching character.

comparisons.title: Portulacaceae vs Talinaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be succulent and often have 2 sepals + 5 petals. Portulaca commonly has a partly inferior ovary and circumscissile capsule; Talinum has a superior ovary and a capsule opening by longitudinal valves, commonly 3.

comparisons.title: Portulacaceae vs Caryophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Caryophyllaceae usually has opposite non-succulent leaves, a more conventional 5-sepal/5-petal flower, and capsules opening by teeth or valves rather than a Portulaca lid.

visual_lesson.caveat: Succulence alone is not diagnostic. Confirm the reproductive architecture.

reconciliation_2026_10_14.look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: on a Portulaca flower, label the TWO sepals and the 4–6 petals; note succulent stem/leaf and possible axillary hairs, but treat these as supporting. Find the superior-to-semi-inferior ovary position in side view and, decisively, a ripe MANY-SEEDED capsule splitting transversely around its middle (circumscissile): separate lid above and seed-bearing cup below. Two sepals or succulence alone cannot establish Portulacaceae.
reconciliation_2026_10_14.local_confusion: SIDE-BY-SIDE: Talinaceae/Talinum shares succulent habit and 2 sepals/usually 5 petals; a mature Talinum capsule splits lengthwise into commonly 3 valves, NOT a Portulaca lid. Caryophyllaceae typically has opposite nodes and capsules opening by apical teeth/valves (but Paronychia has one-seeded utricles); Amaranthaceae usually has tiny bracteate flowers with 1-seeded utricles, and some Amaranthus fruits also open by a transverse lid—so the WORD 'circumscissile' alone is not a family test. Count seeds, inspect flower whorls and compare the entire capsule architecture.
reconciliation_2026_10_14.photo_handoff: THREE POOL TAXA, ONE GENUS: Portulaca oleracea, P. pilosa, P. umbraticola. Route to Portulaca by 2-sepal flower + many-seeded lid capsule, then leave species distinctions to genus/species lessons (axillary hair tufts, leaf shape, capsule/seed detail need matched verified views).
